title: Command reference
heading: Command reference
text: Command reference Every riskwren command. This page is written from the program itself, so it always matches the version it ships with. Run commands with uv run riskwren … from the project directory. Options that come before the command apply to all of them: riskwren [-h] [--version] [-c FILE] [-v | -q] COMMAND ...

title: Command reference
heading: Commands
text: Command What it does riskwren init Set up a new installation riskwren serve Run the web server riskwren demo Build a fictional organization to explore riskwren db Look after the database schema riskwren users Manage accounts from the command line riskwren verify Check that the history has not been altered riskwren check-dossier Check that a dossier is whole and unchanged riskwren frameworks See and load what the organization is held to riskwren program Move the program between installations riskwren backup Back the whole installation up to one file riskwren restore Restore a backup into an empty database riskwren doctor Check that this installation is healthy riskwren jobs See scheduled work

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren init
text: Write a configuration file if there is none, create the data home, create or upgrade the database, and create the first administrator if there is none. Safe to run again. Option Meaning --force overwrite an existing configuration file --admin-email EMAIL create the first administrator with this address --admin-name NAME the first administrator's name --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking --program KIND the program to start from: research-institute (the default), academic-medical-center, university, or nonprofit

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren serve
text: Run RiskWren's web server. It refuses to start on a database whose schema is behind; run riskwren db upgrade first. Option Meaning --host address to listen on (default: from the configuration) --port PORT port to listen on (default: from the configuration) --workers WORKERS server processes (default: from the configuration) --reload restart when the code changes (development) --demo-on-network let a demo organization listen beyond this machine (anyone who reaches it can sign in as its sample people)

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren demo
text: Build the Northmere Institute for Health Research, a fictional organization with two years of history, in its own directory. Everything in it is made by the same code the app uses. Start it with the command it prints. Option Meaning PATH where to build it (default: ./demo) --seed SEED a different number gives a different Northmere --port PORT the port its server will use (default: 8020) --force rebuild a demo that is already there

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren db
text: Look after the database schema.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren db upgrade
text: Apply any migrations the database has not had. Export first: an upgrade cannot be undone except by restoring.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren db current
text: Show which migration the database is at, and which this version expects. Exits with 1 when they differ.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users
text: Manage accounts from the command line: for setting up, and for getting back in when nobody can sign in. Everyday account management is in the app, under Admin. Changes made here are recorded in the history as made at the command line.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users add
text: Add an account. It asks for a password unless --password-stdin or --invite is given. Option Meaning EMAIL the email address the person signs in with --name the person's name --title their job title --role ROLE a role: admin, manager, assessor, auditor, steward=unit:CODE, or leader=unit:CODE,limit:RATING; manager and assessor may also take unit:CODE (may be repeated) --unit CODE a unit they work in, by code (may be repeated) --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking --invite add them without a password: they can be named on records now, and sign in once they are given a password or use single sign-on

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users list
text: List every account with its status and roles.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users disable
text: Stop an account signing in and end its sessions. Its history is kept, and what the person alone answered for passes to the steward of its unit until someone is named for good. The last active administrator cannot be disabled. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users enable
text: Let a disabled account sign in again. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users reset-password
text: Give an account a new password and end its sessions. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users roles
text: Show an account's roles, or with --set replace the roles granted in RiskWren. Roles mapped from an identity provider are left alone. The last active administrator cannot lose that role. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address --set ROLE a role: admin, manager, assessor, auditor, steward=unit:CODE, or leader=unit:CODE,limit:RATING; manager and assessor may also take unit:CODE (may be repeated); with none, removes every role

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren verify
text: Recompute the hash chain over every event in the history and report the first one that does not hold, then check every published version of a document, and every leadership report, against the fingerprint the history took when it was published or issued. Exits with 1 if any does not hold.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren check-dossier
text: Check a dossier taken from RiskWren: every file its manifest lists is there with the size and SHA-256 it lists, nothing else is, and the manifest's fingerprint is its own. Needs no database. Exits with 1 if it does not hold. Option Meaning FILE the dossier's ZIP file

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks
text: A framework is a source of requirements: a public standard, a regulation, an agreement's terms. Four public ones ship with RiskWren and are loaded at installation. Others are loaded from a pack file, or entered in the app.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks list
text: List every framework.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks load
text: Load a framework from a pack file, or the built-in ones that are missing. A pack is checked whole first and refused whole if anything is wrong. Option Meaning FILE the pack to load, or the key of one that ships to be loaded on request, such as hipaa-breach, nist-privacy, nist-800-53-r4, or iso-27001 --builtin load the built-in frameworks not yet here, and the publishers' mappings for those that are --dry-run check the pack, and load nothing

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks show
text: Show a framework's publisher, version, license, and source. Option Meaning KEY the framework's key, such as nist-csf

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks text
text: For a framework that ships as its codes alone, such as iso-27001, load the titles and text from a copy your organization holds a license to: a CSV file with the columns code, title, and text. The words stay in this installation and in its backups; no pack or export carries them. A row with an empty title and text takes that requirement's words away. Option Meaning KEY the framework's key, such as iso-27001 FILE the CSV file of code, title, and text

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren program
text: The program is everything a risk and compliance team configures: vocabularies, the risk categories and their appetite, the scoring method, cadences, and who may accept what. It lives in the database and moves as one file.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren program export
text: Write the whole program as one JSON document, to a file or to standard output. Option Meaning --output , -o FILE write to this file

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren program import
text: Load a program pack. The whole pack is checked first, and nothing is loaded unless all of it can be. A new scoring method is published as a new version; assessments already made keep the version they were made under, and every open risk is read again from what was loaded: its ratings, its standing, and its next review. Option Meaning FILE the pack to load, or the name of a starter program: research-institute, academic-medical-center, university, or nonprofit --dry-run say what would change, and change nothing

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren backup
text: Write every table, every stored file, and a manifest of their fingerprints to one file, as of one moment, while the server goes on running. The file restores into SQLite or PostgreSQL. Keep it somewhere safe: it holds everything. Option Meaning FILE the file to write, which must not exist

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren restore
text: Load a backup into an empty database and data home, then check every table, every file, and the history against it. To move between SQLite and PostgreSQL, back up from one and restore into the other. Use the same version of RiskWren that took the backup, then upgrade. Option Meaning FILE the backup to restore --describe only say what the backup holds

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren doctor
text: Check the configuration, the data home, the database and its schema, and the history. Exits with 1 if anything must be fixed. Option Meaning --production also check what matters before real people rely on it: the https address, the database, a recent backup, a second administrator, email, and that it is not a demo

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren jobs
text: Scheduled work brings risks up to date with the calendar, sends reminders, and sends email where that is set up. The server does this by itself while it runs. These commands are for seeing how it is going, and for running it from a scheduled task where the server's own scheduler is turned off.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren jobs run
text: Run every job that is due. With a job's name, run that one now whether or not it is due. A job another process is running is left to it. Option Meaning JOB one job to run now

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren mail
text: Email is optional. Where it is set up, the server sends it by itself while it runs. These commands are for testing the settings and for sending by hand.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren mail run
text: Queue notices and daily summaries, and send what is waiting. Exits with 1 if a message could not be sent.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren mail test
text: Send one message now to the account with this address, and say whether the mail server accepted it. Option Meaning EMAIL the account to send it to

title: Changelog
text: Wave 9, Adoption : what an organization that has never seen RiskWren needs to install it, make it its own, and run it in production. An installation backs up to one file that restores into SQLite or PostgreSQL, and has been measured with many records and many people at once. It deploys as a container with PostgreSQL or as a locked-down service, and says what stands between it and production. It starts from a program written for a research institute, an academic medical center, a university, or a nonprofit, takes fields and words of the organization's own, and lets other systems in with tokens that act as a role and tell them what happens with signed webhooks. heading: Known limits

Email has been tested against a test server, not through an organization's mail service. Two records that are the same thing can be found, and not yet merged.
